title: One Setting, Any Scene: Tuning-Free Model-Size Control for 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Deploying a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene on a phone, a headset or a web page is governed by how many primitives the model contains, yet no current training method lets a practitioner specify that number. Mask-based pruning, the leading in-training approach, controls it only indirectly through a constant sparsity weight, so the delivered size emerges from that constant, the scene and the densification schedule together. Across thirteen standard scenes at the published setting we measure final sizes spanning a factor of 7.8. We replace the constant with a dual variable driven by the constraint that the live population equal a budget supplied by the user. Plain dual ascent is not sufficient, for a reason that has not previously been reported: although masked primitives keep receiving gradients and are therefore assumed to be recoverable, in practice they are not. With deletion disabled and the sparsity pressure released to effectively zero, the live population ends 16,600 primitives below where it started, recovering only about 6,500 against a deficit of 207,000. Masking is a one-way door, so an overshooting controller can never recover, and we measure undershoots of up to 36%. Approaching the budget from above and landing with a single terminal projection removes the failure entirely: one setting, applied unchanged to all thirteen scenes at two seeds, delivers exactly the requested number of primitives every time. A paired comparison bounds the quality difference to [−0.076, +0.085] dB while models are 2.2× smaller and 1.40× faster to render.
